chunks: Al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yunus ibn Bahman, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A Christian relative of mine sent me as a gift roasted chickens and chicks, and prepared for me falawudhajah (a type of dish). Should I eat it? He said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.فَالُوذَجَةَ: A type of prepared dish or stew
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat food gifted by Christians in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of consuming roasted poultry and prepared dishes gifted by a Christian relative, affirming that their food is considered pure (*tahir*) and edible. This ruling highlights the Shia distinction between the general permissibility of 'People of the Book' food and specific conditions of preparation, emphasizing that gifts from non-Muslims do not inherently render the food impure or forbidden.
